messages.author: 3200d1e2cd5f9d67
messages.subject: Error in Model
parts:
Hi
I've have created a model which keeps giving me error messages in Lavaan. The model I've created has four latent variables (BURDEN, APPROPO, CONCERN and INVOLVE). All of the variables beginning with DP are measured variables. Here is the model:

myModel <- ‘ BURDEN =~ DP4A_SPEND + DP4B_INCON + DP4C_NUM + DP4D_BURDEN + DP4E_TOOMANY
APPROPO =~ DP5A_FEEL + DP5B_STOP + DP5C_DOSE + DP5D_NOT_WORK + DP5E_SE
CONCERN =~ DP6A_RELUCT + DP6B_WORRIED + DP6C_STRESS + DP6D_GIVEUP
INVOLVE =~ DP7A_REASON + DP7B_LIST + DP7C_KNOW + DP7D_DECISION + DP7E_ASK’

The error says Unexpected input in INVOLVE. Or sometimes the error says the object DP6A_RELUCT  does not exist (when I can look in the dataset and the variable clearly does exist). I cannot proceed further to do a cfa analysis.

Can anyone suggest what I am doing wrong?

Thank you.
Marjorie

messages.author: 08146071976f553f
messages.subject: Re: Error in Model
parts:
Hello Marjorie,

Perhabs the problem is not in the formulation of your model, but in the code used to fit your model. Could you provide the functions you used?
What happens if you get rid of INVOLVE. Do you still get the error?

Cheers, Guido

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error in Model
parts:
I think this is a copy/paste problem.  R does not recognize "fancy quotes" (which have little curls to make the text pretty, automatically/annoyingly converted in Word), only the plain-text single- or double-quotation marks.  Try this:

myModel <- ' BURDEN =~ DP4A_SPEND + DP4B_INCON + DP4C_NUM + DP4D_BURDEN + DP4E_TOOMANY

APPROPO =~ DP5A_FEEL + DP5B_STOP + DP5C_DOSE + DP5D_NOT_WORK + DP5E_SE
CONCERN =~ DP6A_RELUCT + DP6B_WORRIED + DP6C_STRESS + DP6D_GIVEUP
INVOLVE =~ DP7A_REASON + DP7B_LIST + DP7C_KNOW + DP7D_DECISION + DP7E_ASK

'

Terrence D. Jorgensen

messages.author: 3200d1e2cd5f9d67
messages.subject: Re: Error in Model
parts:
Thank you to Guido and Terrence. The model has now run successfully although I'm not sure why. I did change the fancy quotes, Terrence, but I had put plain quotes in earlier and it hadn't run then (but it did now - who can figure?).

Thank you Guido, in the end I didn't need to run it again without one of the latent variables as I got it to work. In answer to your question about what function I was using, I'm afraid I'm not sure. I was trying to use the 'user-friendly' version of Lavaan where I didn't need to specify anything - it would add in everything else as a default (see Roussell paper, p.10).

Thank you both for your help.
Marjorie
